title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measures the marginal detection benefit of automated sandboxed emulation over a strong deterministic validator for LLM-generated network-configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) we evaluated Npairs = 720 intent→configuration tasks produced by the declared model (gpt-5-mini). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. The run-level accounting records 721 model calls (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call), and the single guarded-only detection aligns with that single downstream repair-stage invocation. The observed aggregate effect is far below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, artifact-grounded quantitative results and diagnostics, an explanation for the negligible guarded benefit in this setting, explicit reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle, and concrete limitations and recommendations for follow-up work.

sections.introduction:
Generative models that translate operator intent into executable network configuration are being proposed as components of NetOps and AIOps workflows. Operational safety for such agentic pipelines typically depends on surrounding deterministic validators, formal verifiers, and sandboxed execution rather than on the language model in isolation [1], [2]. Prior work advocates generate→validate→repair architectures and prototype runtime emulation, but quantitative cross-vendor evaluations of the marginal value added by sandboxed emulation over a strong static validator are limited. We therefore posed the confirmatory research question that guided our preregistered study: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired-binary experiment executed end-to-end (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). (2) Artifact-grounded quantitative results on Npairs = 720 showing a vanishing aggregate guarded benefit in this setting. (3) Detailed diagnostics tying the single guarded-only detection to run accounting and a focused failure-analysis that explains why the guarded stage produced negligible marginal coverage. (4) Reproducibility pointers and an explicit discussion of limitations and regimes where guarded stages remain necessary.
sections.related_work: Surveys and recent system papers document growing interest in LLM-enabled NetOps and emphasize workflow-centred mitigations—deterministic validators, verifiers, and sandboxed emulation—to reduce operational risk [1], [2]. Tool and prototype work in NetOps and adjacent program-verification domains demonstrates generate→validate→repair patterns and shows that emulation or formal analysis can reveal runtime failures missed by purely static checks [2], [3]. Empirical studies in software and code-generation domains report that LLMs can produce incorrect outputs and that external verifiers reduce error prevalence, but results vary substantially by task, validator strength, and dataset construction. Our experiment operationalizes a narrowly scoped instance of these recommendations by measuring the marginal guarded-stage detection gain against a strong deterministic validator on a synthetic, parser-validated task bank.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental design. We froze a machine-readable preregistration prior to execution (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). Design: paired-binary with shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair a single initial model generation (shared) supplies the candidate used by both the baseline and guarded analyses. Planned confirmatory Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Power planning used a preregistered minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 (20 percentage points) and an approximate paired-binary calculation to target ≈80% power under conservative baseline assumptions.

Task bank. Confirmatory items were synthetic intent→configuration tasks from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family. Tasks cover abstracted vendor-CLI families and several small topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance per the preregistered inclusion rules; parser failures were handled by the deterministic missingness policy (up to two automatic reseeds; no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred in the confirmatory set).

Model, prompting, and sampling semantics. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider entry recorded as openai_responses). Execution settings recorded in model_configuration.json declared max_output_tokens = 2000; temperature = null. Important semantical clarification: temperature = null in the recorded configuration indicates that no explicit temperature parameter was provided in the provider request; it does not imply deterministic sampling or temperature=0. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: a single sampled initial candidate per pair was reused for both baseline and guarded analyses. Therefore any between-condition discordance can arise only from (a) guarded-stage emulation observations that reveal a violation not covered by the static validator or (b) a permitted downstream repair-stage model call recorded in the run accounting.

Validator and guarded pipeline. Baseline condition: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applied full intent-constraint checks (syntax, workflow ordering constraints, required-field presence). Guarded condition: the same deterministic validator followed by an automated sandboxed emulation harness that executes the candidate against an emulated topology and observes runtime behaviors beyond static rule checks. The repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model call per task; the run-level provider accounting shows exactly one repair invocation in the confirmatory execution.

Analysis plan and implementation. Analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. We report the exact McNemar two-sided test and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness and exclusions followed the preregistered deterministic policies and are summarized in the archived missingness report.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (complete paired set, Npairs = 720). Contingency counts from the archived paired contingency table are: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These numerical values are reported exactly as produced by the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor.

Run accounting and attribution of the single discordant pair. The authoritative execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation record show model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared_initial generations + 1 repair-stage call) and stage accounting with a single repair-stage invocation. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the only plausible mechanisms for the single guarded-only detection are (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation or (ii) the recorded repair-stage invocation. Readers can locate the specific per-episode entry that demonstrates the discordant outcome by searching the archived per-episode results file for the single entry where baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1. The archived per-episode raw-results and the reconciliation artifact are stored in the execution bundle at execution/raw_results.jsonl and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; those files contain the pair_id and the per-episode validator/emulation traces needed to verify the attribution. (For reproducibility: execution/raw_results.jsonl is the primary per-episode archive referenced by the execution manifest; the analysis bundle also contains analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv.)

Missingness and compliance. The preregistered missingness policy led to complete_pair_count = 720; there were no irrecoverable parser failures or preregistration deviations affecting the primary estimand. The analysis artifacts (missingness summary and contamination summary) archived alongside the paired contingency table corroborate these statements.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded benefit negligible in aggregate? The archived artifacts and run accounting support three artifact-grounded explanatory factors: (1) ceiling effect — deterministic_netops_validator_v5 provided near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and explicit semantic misconfigurations present in the synthetic task bank; this is evidenced by the baseline success rate of 0.9986 and the validator traces archived per-episode showing validator_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and violation_count = 0 for the vast majority of items. (2) task curation — the confirmatory tasks were parser-validated synthetic items constructed to exercise workflow policies but not to be adversarial or noisy; such construction concentrates items inside the validator's rule set and inflates static-check coverage. (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics — identical initial generations across conditions strictly limit discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or permitted repair calls; the run-level accounting shows exactly one repair-stage call, which aligns with the single n10 discordant count.

Operational implications. When a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs closely match validator coverage, adding sandboxed emulation can yield negligible marginal detection gains at the aggregate level. This finding should not be generalized: in operational regimes with noisy inputs, adversarial mutations, stateful protocol interactions, or validator gaps, guarded runtime checks and higher-fidelity emulation can be decisive. Our artifacts support this conditional interpretation: the per-episode validator traces and emulation outputs archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl show numerous examples where emulation duplicates validator findings but few where emulation alone discovered a violation.

Sensitivity to design choices. The study was powered for a preregistered minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20. The realized discordant counts (n10 = 1) imply the experiment did not observe an effect remotely close to that target; the observed CI upper bound (≈0.00417) makes clear that large aggregated guarded benefits are absent for this task bank/validator in this experimental regime but does not imply absence across other regimes. We therefore frame our contribution as a narrowly scoped, fully preregistered measurement and diagnostic exercise rather than a general claim about all LLM+validator pipelines.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by automated sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Aggregated over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline yielded a negligible detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. The run-level accounting shows a single repair-stage invocation that corresponds to the single guarded-only detection; because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the archived per-episode traces and reconciliation record permit independent verification of that mapping (see execution/raw_results.jsonl and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json in the execution bundle). We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task-bank design and recommend targeted follow-up work on adversarial and multi-vendor task banks, multiple validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value.

Key elements (concise): requested model = "gpt-5-mini" (provider entry: openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; preregistration id = f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e. Initial master-prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution accounting: the authoritative execution manifest records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) and stage accounting with a single repair-stage invocation; the execution manifest and per-episode archives (execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv) are archived as the canonical reproducibility bundle referenced by the run. Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline performed literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. The archived execution bundle contains full prompts, responses, validator and emulation traces, and analysis artifacts for independent verification.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) constrain discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls; this design choice isolates the guarded-stage contribution but reduces variance produced by independent generation.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; scale and vendor nuances could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrow negative (near-zero) finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Although we provide archive pointers for independent verification (execution/raw_results.jsonl and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json), reviewers seeking the explicit per-episode pair_id corresponding to the single n10 discordant entry may locate it within execution/raw_results.jsonl by searching for the unique episode where baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; that per-episode record contains the pair_id and the validator/emulation traces needed to confirm the mapping.
